overview: The subcommittee reviewed trauma-informed behavioral health initiatives and student mental health supports, followed by a discussion on fostering authentic peer friendships for students with disabilities. Members also voted to develop universal accessibility and accommodations language across district and municipal programs.

items.title: Behavioral Health and Trauma-Informed Schools
items.summary: Director Schulman outlined current staff trauma training and upcoming student workshops with The NAN Project, prompting discussion on whether to mandate annual mental health professional development and how best to survey and alleviate pandemic-related student stress.

items.title: Special Education and Friendship Building
items.summary: The committee examined resources for building authentic peer friendships and inclusion for students with disabilities, discussing existing models such as the high school's Common Ground group, Best Buddies, and Epic Service Warriors.

items.title: Universal Accessibility Language and Document Access
items.summary: The subcommittee voted to draft universal language ensuring accessibility and accommodations across school and city recreation, sports, and after-school programs, while also reviewing ways to make committee resources and minutes publicly accessible.
